chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Sayf, from his father Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: How did the ghusl of Friday become obligatory? He said: “Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, completed the obligatory salat by means of the supererogatory salat, and He completed the obligatory fasting by means of the supererogatory fasting, and He completed the wudu (ablution) of the supererogatory by means of the Friday ghusl, for whatever there may be in that of forgetfulness, deficiency in performance, or shortcoming.”

key_terms.صَلَاةَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory salat prescribed by Allah
key_terms.صَلَاةِ النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory salat that completes deficiencies in obligatory prayer
key_terms.غُسْلُ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the ritual bath of Friday discussed here as a legislated act connected to worship
key_terms.نُقْصَانٍ: shortcoming or deficiency in the act
key_terms.وَاجِباً: obligatory or binding in the sense asked about by the narrator
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing associated with prayer

ai.seo_question: Why is Friday ghusl considered obligatory in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the function of Friday ghusl as a completion and rectification for shortcomings connected with acts of worship. It presents a broader devotional principle: Allah supplements deficiencies in obligatory acts through legislated supererogatory and purificatory practices.
